School & learning

sentence noun

in grammar

also sentences, complete sentence, full sentence

classical

Hor. S. 1.10.9: ut currat sententia
Quint. 9.3.45: initia et clausulae sententiārum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 27, 34, 248

sententia, sententiae f.

noun, first declension

a sentence

A thought put into words, and so a sentence (Lewis & Short); also an opinion, a vote, a maxim. Sentence by sentence, per singulās sententiās; to answer in full sentences, tōtīs sententiīs respondēre (Traupman 27, 28).

Other words

  • periodus, periodī f. — a period, a long rounded sentence

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 204 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. sentence

    The orator’s rounded sentence, for which Cicero also says ambitus, circuitus, comprehēnsiō (Or. 204, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • est brevitāte opus, ut currat sententia, neu sē inpediat verbīs lassās onerantibus aurīs

    you need brevity, so that the sentence runs on and does not get tangled in words that weigh on tired earsHor. S. 1.10.9–10

  • ita verba in variīs sententiīs locīs suīs posita et crēbrō audīta quārum rērum signa essent paulātim conligēbam

    so, hearing words again and again, each in its place in different sentences, little by little I worked out what things they stood forAug. Conf. 1.8.13

See also word, grammar, verb, noun, read aloud.
